emma: quick sync — ran a quick three-way micro-bench (A100 / H100 / L40S) for small-batch=1, seq=512, kv-cache warm. seeing weird p99 spike on H100 only. results pasted below. any obvious suspects? :thinking:

raj: can you drop the exact command and the raw p95/p99 numbers? helps rule out measurement differences. :eyes:

emma: sure — command:
```bash
./run_bench --model gpt-small --hw A100,H100,L40S --batch 1 --seq 512 --kv_cache=warm --iters 200 --collect p95,p99
```
raw: A100 p95=42ms p99=72ms; H100 p95=48ms p99=160ms; L40S p95=45ms p99=74ms

noah: H100 p99 160ms with warm cache is suspicious. did you pin the CUDA driver/GC flags the same across rigs? sometimes driver mismatches + power capping shows up as microbursts.

emma: all infra images use the same container tag (infra/bench:2026-03-08). driver versions: A100 & L40S -> 545.85, H100 -> 545.85 as well per nvidia-smi. power cap = default across all.

sara: did you run any other workloads concurrently on the H100 node? interference can cause tail-bloat.

emma: I ran overnight sweeps earlier but verified node was idle. I also checked dmesg — saw repeated kernel WARN about nvlink peer timeouts around the runs (snippet):
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=0, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679001] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 43, GPU fell off the bus during reset
```

raj: oof. Xid 31/43 indicates a recoverable GPU reset. that can definitely explain p99 spikes. which H100 instance type was this (cloud SKU)?

emma: h100-p4d-standard-1 (custom rack). I've flagged with infra but wanted to see if perf team sees any software-level causes first.

perf-bot: bench-run summary uploaded to /artifacts/bench/1798765432/ — compare CSVs available.

noah: ok two threads to run in parallel: (1) infra: confirm HW stable + NV drivers/hotfixes and check for firmware updates; (2) runtime: reproduce with tracing enabled to profile queuing / kernel stalls. I can add a lightweight perf trace if you give me the reproducer command.

emma: starting a repro with TRACE=kernel,queue and smaller iters now. command:
```bash
TRACE=kernel,queue ./run_bench --model gpt-small --hw H100 --batch 1 --seq 512 --iters 50 --log-level debug > h100-trace.log 2>&1
```

sara: pinging @infra-team — can you check the H100 host (ID h100-17) for ECC errors, temp, and PSUs around 2026-03-08 03:00 UTC?

ops-bot: @infra-team notified: ticket INF-4821 created (h100-17 nvlink/xid).

raj: in parallel, try toggling our small-batch kernel flag: set ENV USE_SMALL_KERN=1 vs 0. kernel selection for tiny batches is different and we saw regressions when kernel fallback path triggers.

emma: good call — will run USE_SMALL_KERN=0/1 and report. also adding --no-prefetch to rule out cache prefetcher interactions.

noah: if repro shows consistent resets, capture `nvidia-bug-report.sh` and upload. if it only happens under our runtime, we should instrument the allocator and kernel launch timelines.

emma: updated bench runs: with USE_SMALL_KERN=1 p99 on H100 dropped to ~78ms (closer to others). with USE_SMALL_KERN=0 p99 back to ~155ms. seems like kernel selection path matters. dumping traces now and will attach perf-bot artifacts.

raj: nice find. that narrows it to kernel fallback causing inefficient kernels on H100. can you open a PR that forces small-kernel for tiny batches and add a feature flag + test? keep fallback for other scenarios.

emma: will do. I'll also coordinate with infra for the nvlink/WARNs since those resets could mask other issues. thanks folks. :thumbsup:

sara: awesome. next steps: 1) emma PR w/ flag + benchmark artifact, 2) infra to investigate Xid and firmware, 3) perf to add targeted kernel profiling for H100 tiny-batch path. I can own the follow-up doc.

emma: assigning follow-ups in the ticket. I'll post links when PR + traces are up.
